kurz: Herbs and spices carry their flavour in volatile aroma compounds: heat, fat and time decide how much of it reaches the food.
bild_im_kopf: Like perfume: a touch works wonders, left open it fades.
was_passiert: The aroma compounds sit in tiny oil glands in leaves and seeds. Many dissolve better in fat than in water. Fresh herbs lose them with long cooking, while dried [[gewuerze|spices]] only release them in heat and fat.
warum_wichtig: When and how you season often matters more than how much.
faustregeln: Woody herbs such as rosemary and thyme early, tender ones such as basil and parsley at the end.
Toast whole spices briefly in fat before liquid goes in.
